title: Ashaveri Inference Receipt (JSON twin of the CBOR/COSE wire format)
description: Display-only projection of the signed COSE_Sign1 receipt. The CBOR bytes are canonical; this JSON form is never signed directly. The payload branch describes the three versions the CDDL defines: receipt-v1's thirteen fields, receipt-v2, which is those same fields plus the marking attestation, and receipt-v3, which is v2's fourteen plus the stamp disclosure, the captured collateral validity anchor and the per-item list. Each branch is closed, so a member its version does not name is a refusal here exactly as it is in the CDDL and in the parser. Closure is not one level: the payload map and the six nested inside it, `meas`, `att`, `tok`, `mk`, `sd` and `cva`, are closed, so a member one of them does not name is refused at that level too rather than read here and dropped on the way to a verifier. `itm` is an array rather than a map, and its elements are the closed `itemStamp` map below, so a member an entry does not name is refused at that level as well. The payload branches refuse an unnamed member through `unevaluatedProperties`, which is the keyword that reaches through their `allOf`, and the nested definitions through `additionalProperties`, which is the one that applies where the members are named in the same object. `protectedHeader` carries the three labels the CDDL declares and no more, and this definition carries no closure keyword: the parser reads that map by number and accepts only those three labels, so a document carrying another is refused before any projection of it is built and an unnamed label never arrives here as a field left out, and the parser decodes that map where no floating-point number can appear, because a label written as the float 1.0 takes the map slot of the integer 1 and is no longer distinguishable from it afterwards. The unprotected map is the format's one declared carrier of no claim, outside the signature and outside this projection.

kid.description: sha256 of the Ed25519 public key, hex

payload.description: Exactly one branch per payload version. `v` is which one the document is, and the branches are exclusive on it.

signature.description: Ed25519 signature over the Sig_structure, hex

m.description: SHA-256 for a software deployment, the platform's SHA-384 measurement for a TEE

payloadV1.description: A v1 document and nothing else. The map is closed: `unevaluatedProperties` refuses any member payloadFields and `v` do not name, so a v1 payload cannot carry a marking attestation, and a reader never has to work out what became of a member it did not read.

payloadV2.description: A v2 document and nothing else. The map is closed the same way v1's is: fourteen members are the whole of it, so a member outside this list is a malformed payload rather than a member a reader agreed to forget.

itm.description: One entry per response item, in the order the response put them in, and never an empty list: a run of nothing states nothing, and a stream that sent no data frame is a refusal at issuance rather than an array of zero here. A response that was not streamed is one entry holding the whole body, which may be no bytes at all.

payloadV3.description: A v3 document and nothing else. The map is closed the same way the other two are: seventeen members are the whole of it, the fourteen a v2 document carries plus the disclosure, the anchor and the item list, so a member outside this list is a malformed payload rather than a member a reader agreed to forget.

sch.description: a label from the marking-scheme registry. Not an enum here because the CDDL admits any tstr: the registry this package reads is `none` and `provenance-v1`, and it refuses a label outside those two as UNSUPPORTED_SCHEME rather than this twin deciding the format.

d.description: sha256 of the marked region exactly as it appears in the response, not of the whole response. For `sch: "none"` the region is empty and this is the digest of no bytes.

marking.description: The marking attestation, one map for the two versions that carry it: v2 makes it required and v3 carries it unchanged, so neither branch can drift from the other on the same two members.

name.description: what the source that read the issuance instant calls itself, as its owner names it

unc.description: Seconds that source declares it can be away from the instant it names. `null` is the source saying nobody measured how far away it is, which is a different statement from `0` and is refused by a policy that demands a bound; an absent member would be readable as either, so the field is required and its two readings are values.

stampDisclosure.description: Where one signed instant came from, in the source's own words. The instant itself is not here, because it is already signed once beside the nonce that dates the document.

col.description: the signed collateral the bytes were appraised against

val.description: the validity context they were appraised in

collateralValidityAnchor.description: What became of the two pieces of appraisal context, captured when they were taken in. Both halves are required because an anchor that defaults a missing half to a pass is not an anchor.

collateralSlot.description: One of two shapes, told apart by `p`: the context this anchor holds, which is a digest and nothing else, or the context it does not, which is a reason and no digest. `oneOf` rather than a list of members because a slot with a digest and a reason is not a third state, and a reader would have to choose which of the two the writer meant.

d.description: sha256 of the bytes exactly as they arrived. No byte count rides beside it, because a count of bytes this document does not hold is a number nothing can check it against, and no verdict, because whether the collateral verifies is a reader's question asked with its own pins.

p.description: Which of the two absences this is: the source had nothing to give, or this collector did not take in what was there. One is a statement about the world and the other about us, and a record that could not tell them apart could be read as either.

r.description: In one line, the collector's own words for why there are no bytes. Required, because an absence nobody explained is a hole rather than a state.

t.description: unix seconds the source named by `sd` read when this item's bytes were framed

d.description: sha256 of exactly this item's bytes and of none of the framing around them, which is why the item list and the whole-response digest are two statements about one byte string rather than one derivable from the other

itemStamp.description: One response item: its instant and its digest, in the order the response put them in. Chain order is that order and stamp order is `t`; a reader refuses a list where the two disagree.
